attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase used to express that (A) remains in a state of not being done.

attributes.body:
まだ～ていません is a regular expression that combines the adverb まだ, with the conjunction particle て. The て form will be followed by the verb いる in its negative いません (polite), or いない (casual) form. This expression has the meaning of 'to still not have done (A)'.

From these examples, it can be seen that this grammatical structure follows the regular rules of conjugation for the て form.

The grammar point 'Verb[volitional]とする' expresses the speaker's decision or intention to do something, often indicating a plan or goal. In contrast, 'まだ～ていません' is used to express that an action has not yet occurred or a state has not yet been reached, emphasizing the ongoing absence of the action or state.

first_relatable.title: Verb[volitional]とする
first_relatable.meaning: Try to, Attempt to, To be about to

attributes.body: まだ suggests that something remains in a state, or that an action has not yet occurred, similar to the English 'still' or 'not yet.' When used with a verb in the ていません form, it expresses the continued non-occurrence of an action. For example, まだ食べていません means 'I haven't eaten yet' or 'I still haven't eaten.'
